ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence under Article L.561-10 of the French Monetary and Financial Code for any Politically Exposed Persons among shareholders, managers and beneficial owners; systematic screening against the French Asset Recovery and Freezing Commission list, EU consolidated financial sanctions lists and UN Security Council sanctions. For USD-denominated Swift LC/TT wire payments, additional OFAC SDN list screening is required by corresponding-bank policy.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés and the Guichet Unique des Entreprises (procedures.inpi.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name (dénomination sociale) must be expressed in Latin-script characters; any non-Latin source name requires a French transliteration. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing company or protected trademark, and it must indicate the legal form 'SARL' in official documents.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Commissaire aux comptes (reserved for statutory auditors enrolled in recognized professional bodies)
National / République / États (ministerial authorization required due to state-associated suffixes)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In the event of pre-incorporation name rejection, the applicant or its legal representative may file a written and reasoned administrative appeal (recours gracieux) with the INPI director within two months of notification. If confusion with a trademark is alleged, evidence of consent or coexistence may be submitted. Judicial recourse may thereafter be made to the local commercial court (tribunal de commerce) in the registered-office jurisdiction. Where rejection is based on incomplete documentation, the applicant should re-file through the Guichet Unique within the remaining name-availability window after curing all deficiencies.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only through an approved domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) certified by the Préfecture; such virtual office may serve as registered office, but for steel-structure prefab EPC activities a physical operational address is expected for tax and market licensing.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate; approximately 12% risk of unannounced on-site inspection in the first fiscal year by the labour inspectorate, URSSAF, or tax authorities.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II – Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10 (general formation rules), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 and R.223-1 seq. (SARL formation, share capital, contributions, managers); Article 1832 of the French Civil Code (contract of company); applicable enforcement decrees (Décrets d'application) on RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) administered by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office; all formalities are submitted electronically through the INPI Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts constitutifs (Articles of Association) followed by the online immatriculation form (demande d'immatriculation principale au RCS); the definitive legal existence document is the Extrait Kbis (Kbis Registration Extract).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The SARL has no statutory minimum share capital; the stated capital is freely fixed in the articles. At least 20% of cash contributions must be released at subscription, the balance within five years (Article L.223-7, Code de commerce); cash subscriptions must be deposited in a blocked bank account (escrow) until the company is registered and the Kbis delivered; in-kind contributions must be fully paid at once and, where any in-kind contribution exceeds €7,500, must be valued by a commissaire aux apports (contribution auditor).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION ONE – SHARE SUBSCRIPTION. The sole incorporator subscribes for the one hundred (100) equal shares comprising the stated social capital of EUR 10,000. Twenty per cent of the capital is released in cash today into the blocked account; the balance is payable within four years, in accordance with Article L.223-7 of the French Commercial Code. RESOLUTION TWO – REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office is fixed at [Address, France]; the Manager may lease or acquire all premises and rights required. RESOLUTION THREE – APPOINTMENT OF MANAGER. Mr/Ms [Name] is appointed Gérant with full management powers, including representation, banking and contract signature. RESOLUTION FOUR – FORMALITIES. The Manager shall execute all documents, publications and filings for RCS registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability and Legal Identity Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI national trademark database and INFOGREFFE RCS directory consultation; no filing is made at this stage
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify that the intended dénomination sociale is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing RCS trade name, trademark, or prior registered company. Query the INPI trademark database and Infogreffe RCS records; confirm the availability of the legal form SARL and that the corporate object corresponds to the steel-structure EPC activity (Assembly sites typically fall under NAF/APE 4399D, while in-house steel manufacturing uses NAF 2511Z). Prepare a shortlist of three alternative names and record the availability report for later attachment.
required_dossiers: Passport or national identity card and proof of address of each incorporator
INPI and INFOGREFFE company-name and trademark availability search reports
List of three alternative corporate names (recommended)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or the availability search reveals an identical or confusingly similar name, adopt a written decision changing the corporate name and re-run the availability search; a substitute name may be filed without additional state charges where the correction is made before the registration submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Statutory Articles and Statement of Contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French advocate or notary; notarial deed is mandatory where real property is contributed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statuts in French containing the mandatory SARL clauses: legal form, company name, corporate purpose (engineering, manufacture and assembly of prefabricated steel structures), registered office, duration not exceeding 99 years, share capital, table of contributions, rights attached to shares, identity and powers of the manager, share-transfer restrictions, and the annual accounts approval procedure. Execute the statuts by private deed (acte sous seing privé) or notarial deed. If any in-kind contribution exceeds €7,500, appoint a commissaire aux apports to prepare a valuation report; otherwise, obtain the unanimous written acceptance of the valuation by the persons subscribing for the shares. Sign the written statement of subscription (état des actes de souscription).
required_dossiers: Definitive French-language draft of the articles of association (statuts)
Share-capital subscription table, cash contribution receipts and in-kind valuation report where applicable
Identity documents and proof of address of each shareholder and the appointed gérant
Power of attorney if a representative signs on behalf of any shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the legal review or the registry's pre-control identifies a missing or non-compliant statutory clause, execute an amending resolution of the associates before filing; the amendment is attached to the final registration dossier and no new drafting cycle is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Capital Account and Issuance of Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any credit institution established in France, or a notary authorized to receive the funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate account in the name of the company in formation at a French bank or at the notary's guarantee accounts (Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations for notarial deposits). Deposit at least 20% of the cash subscriptions and obtain a bank certificate of deposit (certificat de dépôt des fonds / attestation de blocage) identifying the company name, the total amount received, and the blocked-account status. Ensure that the balance of the stated capital remains payable within the five-year statutory period and that funds will be released only upon presentation of the Kbis registration certificate. For in-kind contributions, confirm full discharge at signature and file the contribution auditor's report.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening and KYC/KYB file (draft statuts, identity of managers, SARL tax status)
Proof of transfer or payment order from each subscriber to the blocked account
Bank-issued certificate of blocked funds in the company's name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank rejects the account opening or the KYB file, correct the documentation and select another EU credit institution in France; the deposit remains escrowed until registration, and the funds are automatically transferred to the company's current account upon Kbis issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Incorporation Notice in an Authorized Legal Announcements Journal (JAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) authorized by the prefecture of the department where the registered office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and submit the avis de constitution containing the mandatory legal mentions: corporate form (SARL), company name, corporate object, share capital, registered office address, duration, names of the manager(s), and the RCS registry town. Provide the JAL editor with the statutory identification details, attach the capital deposit certificate, and pay the insertion fee. Obtain the attestation de parution (proof of publication) once the notice is published.
required_dossiers: Text of the legal announcement (avis de constitution) in the statutorily required format
Bank certificate of deposit of funds
Statement of share subscriptions and in-kind valuations if requested by the JAL editor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the greffe reports a missing or incorrect mandatory mention in the published notice, insert a rectificative announcement (avis rectificatif) in the same or another authorized JAL before the registration is completed; the corrected publication is then submitted to the greffe.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique — operational portals: impots.gouv.fr (professional 'Espace Pro' for enterprises); business formalities and VAT number allocation through the Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr administered by the INPI; commercial registration with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a newly constituted SARL: (1) file the incorporation dossier (statuts, appointment of gérant, beneficial ownership declaration) with the Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), which routes the file to the RCS; (2) upon registration the Greffe/INPI issues the SIREN (9-digit identification) and SIRET (establishment) numbers; (3) the DGFiP automatically allocates the intra-Community VAT number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire, format FR + 2-digit key + SIREN) and notifies the taxpayer via the SIE (Service des Impôts des Entreprises); (4) activate the professional online account (Espace Pro) on impots.gouv.fr; (5) for a non-established foreign entity carrying out taxable operations in France without a fixed establishment, direct VAT registration is filed with the territorial SIE (or via the OSS/non-EU OSS regimes), attaching the foreign certificate of incorporation, proof of economic activity, and statutory identification documents; a fiscal representative (représentant fiscal) is mandatory for non-EU taxable persons in certain cases; processing time is approximately 2 to 4 weeks from complete filing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a SARL is by default subject to corporation tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) at the 25% standard rate (reduced 15% rate for taxable profits up to EUR 42,500 per annum for qualifying small businesses with turnover below EUR 10 million); no pass-through classification is available as a default. Territorial scope (principe de territorialité): IS is levied only on profits attributable to operations carried out in France or to French assets/rights; foreign branch profits are generally outside the French tax net unless the option for worldwide taxation is exercised. Metropolitan France is not a tax-exempt zone, but targeted exemptions apply (e.g., jeune entreprise innovante, zones franches urbaines, stock-option/R&D credit regimes) and specific overseas-zone regimes exist.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or entity classification election exists. Available statutory elections under French law: (1) option for income tax (IR, régime des sociétés de personnes) under CGI art. 239 bis AA for small SARLs whose members are individuals and which meet the revenue thresholds — option is irrevocable for five fiscal years; (2) VAT elections: option for the 'régime réel normal' from the simplified VAT regime, option for the franchise en base exemption within small-business thresholds, and option for VAT payment on debits; (3) fiscal integration election (intégration fiscale, CGI art. 223 A) permitting a parent holding at least 95% of an EU-established French subsidiary to consolidate the IS result of the group; (4) election for the parent-subsidiary regime (régime mère-fille) and for the participation-exemption on disposal gains; (5) hybrid mismatch rules (CGI art. 212 bis, implementing ATAD) apply automatically to deny deductions or include income for mismatched arrangements; no protective election is available to override them for cross-border hybrid structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA) — governed by CGI articles 256 to 289 C, transposing EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For taxable persons established in France, VAT registration is mandatory from the first taxable transaction (no economic turnover threshold). However, the 'franchise en base de TVA' (small business exemption) applies to businesses whose preceding full-year turnover does not exceed EUR 85,000 (supply of goods, 'seuil normal') or EUR 37,500 (supply of services, 'seuil normal'), with 'seuils majorés' of EUR 93,500 and EUR 41,250 respectively where the prior two-year turnover did not exceed the normal thresholds; once the majoré threshold is exceeded, registration becomes compulsory. Non-established EU suppliers exceed the EUR 10,000 cross-border distance-sales threshold into France to trigger registration (Union OSS scheme or standard French registration); non-EU suppliers of digital/electronic services must register or use the Non-Union OSS from the first sale with no threshold; B2B supplies of services by non-established vendors are subject to reverse charge with no French registration required.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing reform (facturation électronique) for domestic B2B transactions is phased in from 1 September 2026 for large enterprises and mid-size companies (ETI), and from 1 September 2027 for small and micro enterprises (PME/TPE). E-invoices must be issued in a structured electronic format (Factur-X, UBL, CII) and transmitted to the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) through an accredited Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP); there is no real-time fiscal clearance, stamping, or prior visa in the Italian SDI model — instead, near-real-time 'e-reporting' of B2C and cross-border transaction data flows to the PPF within one operating day (J+1) via the same pipeline; foreign taxable persons carrying out registrable French transactions must transmit e-reporting data through an appointed PDP or the simplified OSS procedure, subject to API interoperability standards set by the DGFiP.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods outside the EU are VAT-exempt with full right of deduction (effective 0% rate) under CGI art. 262-I-1° and EU Directive art. 146, provided the goods are physically dispatched or transported out of the EU by the supplier or on its behalf within 90 days, evidenced by a validated export customs declaration (DELTA-X, EX/EXA) bearing the MRN. Intra-Community supplies of goods are exempt under CGI art. 262 ter only where the purchaser holds a valid EU VAT identification number and the goods are dispatched to another EU Member State, with the supplier required to obtain confirmation of the counterpart VAT number within one month. Services directly connected with the export operation (international transport, handling, loading, export-related engineering) may be zero-rated under CGI art. 259 and 262-II where the services are effectively and exclusively linked to the exported goods and rendered to a customer established outside France; for the steel structure prefab EPC model, zero-rating is claimable for the prefabricated building components only when title and physical risk transfer outside the EU and the goods do not enter French consumption; assembly services performed at the foreign site remain outside the scope of French VAT under B2B territoriality rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration en Douane EX/EXA lodged via the DELTA-X system, validated with the MRN/R recognises signature and the export summary declaration)
Bill of Lading or contract of carriage (B/L or sea waybill, CMR consignment note, CIM rail waybill, or ATA carnet, evidencing dispatch outside EU territory)
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank statement or certificate of the authorized intermediary evidencing FX repatriation of export proceeds into France)
Commercial invoice and packing list (including HS codes, gross/net weights, Incoterms, and value declarations)
Intrastat declaration of exchanges of goods (DEB) and the recapitulative statement of intra-Community supplies (with the customer's EU VAT number) for EU-destined deliveries
Incoterms-based proof of risk transfer, insurance certificate or surveyor's report, and port/terminal receipts supporting the physical exit
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to heightened audit scrutiny by the DGFiP's national and territorial VAT verification units and by the customs anti-fraud directorate (DNRED). Any substantive or documentary deficiency triggers immediate VAT reassessment (rappel de TVA) of the exempt amount plus late-payment interest of 0.20% per calendar month (CGI art. 1727) and penalties: 40% for deliberate negligence (mauvaise foi, CGI art. 1729 a) or 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres (manœuvres frauduleuses, CGI art. 1729 b); the penalty base may be increased in cases of occultation of activity. Criminal exposure under CGI art. 1741 for tax fraud reaches 5 years' imprisonment and a EUR 500,000 fine (aggravated to 7 years and EUR 3,000,000 for organised fraud), with an extended 6-year statute of limitation for hidden activities. Customs law (Code des douanes, arts. 414 and 423-2) additionally imposes fines of one to two times the value of the object of the fraud, confiscation of the transport means and goods, and up to 3 years' imprisonment; retrospective clawback may cover the full statutorily reopened prescription period (generally 3 years, extended to 6 years for undisclosed or fraudulent activity).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, acting within the European System of Central Banks led by the European Central Bank; the external relations and capital-movement supervision remit is co-administered by the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury of the Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty), with bank-level prudential enforcement by the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible in France. Article 63 TFEU and the OECD Codes of Liberalisation guarantee unrestricted capital and current-account convertibility; no prior administrative licence is required for trade payments, service and royalty remittances, intra-group flows, dividend distributions, or capital injections. Capital-account liberalisation is tempered only by (i) the French FDI screening regime under Articles L.151-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code and Decree 2019-1590 as amended, which is not triggered for non-sensitive steel structure prefab engineering and assembly (ISIC 4100 / NAICS 236220); (ii) EUR 10,000 cash cross-border declaration duties and Banque de France balance-of-payments statistical reporting applied automatically by resident banks; and (iii) profit remittance friction of a tax nature rather than an exchange-control nature. Dividends paid by the SARL to non-resident shareholders attract a 25% domestic withholding tax, reduced by EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive implementation (0% subject to conditions) and by applicable double tax treaties through refund procedures. The practical remittance pathway therefore requires corporate formality compliance (general meeting decision, certified financial statements where required, tax residency certificates and Form 2561/2777 filing where applicable), not administrative exchange authorisation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or conversion requirement exists for export receipts. A French exporter may retain receivables in euro or in any foreign currency indefinitely at any conversion ratio, and may use the proceeds directly for operational disbursements or within its FX risk-management policy. The applicable statutory obligations are: (i) export invoices and customs declarations to the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (Intrastat for intra-EU dispatches and extra-EU export declarations); (ii) the servicing bank's balance-of-payments reporting to the Banque de France, which statutorily codes all cross-border receipts and payments; and (iii) Tracfin reporting under Article L.561-15 of the French Monetary and Financial Code where trade-based money-laundering indicators are detected. Treasury records must therefore preserve the SWIFT MT103 advices, bills of lading, mill test certificates, packing lists, and VAT export-exemption evidence to substantiate each export receipt in a tax or AML review.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High but structurally limited. Under PSD2 and the Electronic Money Directive (2009/110/EC), only an EEA-authorised Electronic Money Institution or Payment Institution duly passported into France with the ACPR may lawfully provide corporate payment accounts to the SARL. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., UK-only, Caribbean, Singapore-licensed, or UAE-based multi-currency wallets) cannot open a compliant French payment account; they may act solely as unregulated software access layers over an underlying authorised bank, which undermines their treasury usefulness. Furthermore, for the SARL's share capital, French company law requires an attestation de dépôt de fonds issued by a licensed credit institution (or a notaire acting as escrow agent); an EMI is not a credit institution and cannot lawfully certify capital deposits. EMI rails are therefore acceptable for small operational disbursements, petty expenses, and salary payments, but must never be positioned as the statutory escrow or as the primary trade-settlement lane for the EPC treasury.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French AML law (Articles L.561-5 et seq. of the Monetary and Financial Code) and ACPR guidance permit remote video-identification, and no absolute statutory mandate requires all directors to appear physically. In market practice, however, Tier-1 universal banks impose a mandatory in-person KYC interview at a French branch or with a bank-accredited representative for any non-resident corporate structure using external managers, so the SARL's non-resident ownership profile will trigger at least one physical attendance by the duly authorised gérant or the holder of a notarised power of attorney. A fully remote opening is realistically possible only through French FinTech banks and certain EMIs with simplified KYC workflows. The recommended path is therefore hybrid: apostilled corporate deeds, certified passport copies and a face-to-face compliance meeting for the first account generation, followed by digital signing of subsequent mandates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO chain with opaque intermediate holding layers preventing clear identification of ultimate beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group organisational chart signed by the group chief financial officer; certified constitutive documents of each intermediate entity; apostilled passports of all UBOs holding at least 25%; current RCS/INFOGREFFE extract of the SARL; manager's UBO certificate issued within three months; sworn translations of foreign company registers; full share-transfer history from incorporation to date.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between registered office, bank-declared postal address, and actual construction-site operating locations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full-term commercial lease with the legitimate owner; property tax notice and utility invoices bearing the SARL name; site access and photographic documentation; RCS modification filing proving that the declared registered office is the current trade register address; signed reconciliation memo explaining each operating site.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid churning of capital or unexplained incoming third-party payments not named in the underlying commercial contracts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed EPC and subcontracting contracts with a defined payment schedule; commercial invoices and purchase orders; 12-month bank history of each funding shareholder's source account; tax-compliant dividend vouchers where funding derives from profits; corporate resolution authorising the injection; notarial or bank certification of the capital deposit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanction and country-risk flags on steel import corridors, including Chinese, Turkish, or CIS-origin raw material exposures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Country-of-origin certificate per consignment; mill test certificates and batch traceability documents; customs clearance records from the Direction Générale des Douanes; Incoterms 2020 aligned sale contracts; supplier KYC pack with registered address, beneficial owners, and trade licences; completed EU sanctions screening sign-off; written trade-based money-laundering risk assessment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Over-invoicing or under-invoicing indicators typical of trade-based money laundering in fabricated steel structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent price benchmark reports from published steel indices; third-party pre-shipment inspection certificates; quantity surveyor valuation of fabricated tonnage; detailed cost build-up model of the exporter; packing lists and weight certificates submitted to the bank; audited margin analysis for the transaction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound payments routed through an offshore SPV or bridge entity whose economic substance and source of funds cannot be independently verified by the French bank
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FATCA and CRS tax residence certificates of the payer; economic substance or equivalent filing of the SPV jurisdiction; audited financial statements of the payer; certificate of incumbency and register of directors; audited operating-subsidiary source-of-funds proof rather than shelf-company loan documentation; signed compliance indemnity and non-circumvention undertaking.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wiring protocol: (1) open the SARL's blocked capital deposit account (compte bloqué de constitution) with a Tier-1 French bank or before a notaire; (2) the shareholder remits EUR through SWIFT MT103, or SEPA SCT when inside the Single Euro Payments Area, quoting purpose code 'FUND' or 'SHAR' where the bank supports it, with a clear remittance narrative 'Apport en numéraire – constitution de SARL'; (3) the receiving bank issues the attestation de dépôt de fonds required for the RCS filing; (4) after issuance of the Kbis extract, the account is upgraded to the operational current account. The bank will classify the transaction in its Banque de France balance-of-payments report as 'direct investment' (investissement direct), and the file must contain the SARL's SIREN registration, UBO declaration, share subscription agreement, and source-of-funds ledger. No prior French Treasury authorisation applies to non-sensitive steel-structure prefab, but non-EU shareholders must complete the standard declaration des relations financières avec l'étranger whenever the bank's onboarding template requires it.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For payments to EU/EEA suppliers of steel components, freight and subcontract services: SEPA SCT or SWIFT MT103 in EUR with ISO purpose codes 'TRAD', 'SUPP', or 'COST'. For overseas suppliers (China, Turkey, South Korea, Gulf states): (i) cross-border wire transfers in EUR or USD via SWIFT MT103 plus MT202 cover instructions through the correspondent clearing network; (ii) commercial documentary credits governed by the UCP 600, issued via SWIFT MT700 and amended through MT707, where the seller requires payment security; (iii) standby letters of credit and bank guarantees (cautions) issued by the French bank for down-payment advances, performance bonds, and retention obligations of the EPC contract; (iv) documentary collections under URC 522 (documents against payment or acceptance) for low-risk repetitive shipments; and (v) intra-group treasury transfers up to EUR 1 million by SWIFT FIN with code 'CORT' for the cover instruction. All exports and disbursements must be traceable to the underlying steel purchase orders, transport documents, and customs declarations to preserve the KYC defence.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX spot contracts in EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CNH, and EUR/TRY executed directly with a French licensed credit institution for immediate settlement of trade cash flows.

Vanilla FX outright forwards with tenors aligned to firm steel procurement invoices or committed EPC receivables; permitted for hedging within the corporate treasury mandate and subject to the EMIR reporting obligation when concluded above applicable thresholds.
FX swaps (swap de change) between EUR/USD or EUR/GBP for managing temporary cross-currency clearing imbalances; documented under ISDA 2002 or the bank's French-law master agreement as applicable.

Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD and EUR/GBP) for structural hedging of multi-year EPC export receivables or foreign-currency procurement programmes; permitted only on a hedge-designation basis and not for speculative position-taking.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) restricted-currency hedging (e.g., CNY, TRY) where the underlying trade currency is not deliverable in the relevant jurisdiction; acceptable only when executed with an authorised credit institution and directly matched to a commercial exposure.

European currency options (EUR/USD puts and calls) purchased for cash-flow protection around material project milestones; the French corporate treasury policy prohibits writing uncovered options and restricts the instruments to strictly hedged positions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual approval of the financial statements by the shareholders (Ordinary General Meeting) and adoption of the allocation of results
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting of the SARL; executed minutes are kept in the statutory Minutes Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the close of each fiscal year, e.g. 30 June for a 31 December year-end; court-ordered extension possible
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the meeting within the legal deadline exposes the legal representative to a fine of up to EUR 9,000; any interested party may apply to the court to appoint a temporary administrator or to order the meeting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of the annual accounts (balance sheet, income statement, and notes) with the RCS, including the share capital declaration and corporate data confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INPI via the Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval; for a 31 December year-end this is generally no later than 31 July, unless an extension is granted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: After a formal notice from the registrar, an unresolved one-month delay in filing may result in radiation of the company from the RCS; the legal representative is additionally liable to a fine of up to EUR 15,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale, form n° 2065-SD with annexes n° 2050 to 2059)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via online filing at impots.gouv.fr
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December year-end: the second working day after 1 May, generally 3 May; for other fiscal year-ends: on or before the last day of the third month following the close
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a 10% penalty on the net tax due plus monthly late interest of 0.20%; deliberate concealment or manifest bad faith raises the penalty to 40% or 80%.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory for a SARL when two of the following three thresholds are exceeded: total balance sheet greater than EUR 4,000,000; net turnover greater than EUR 8,000,000; average number of employees greater than 50. Appointment is also mandatory for group entities where required by law, and in certain cases on application by a shareholder, the public prosecutor, or the works council.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the Plan Comptable Général (ANC Regulation n° 2014-03); individual accounts of the SARL are prepared in euros and filed as non-consolidated annual accounts. Consolidated financial statements, where required for group structures, may be prepared under French GAAP or IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not impose a standalone annual UBO filing; the RCS beneficial-owner declaration must be updated within 30 days after any change in ultimate ownership or control. Each annual accounts deposit serves as a mandatory checkpoint at which the legal representative confirms the accuracy of the shareholding and UBO data in the RCS record, and any field that has changed is simultaneously updated.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Managers (Registre des Gérants)
Register of Share Transfers (Registre des Mouvements de Titres)
Minutes Register (Registre des Décisions et Assemblées)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax ('impôt sur les sociétés') under Article 219-I CGI, applicable to fiscal years commencing on or after 1 January 2022; reduced 15% rate applies to the first EUR 38,120 of taxable profit for qualifying small enterprises (turnover below EUR 10,000,000, fully paid-up share capital, and at least 75% held by individuals).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% CIT first tranche for SME SARLs; research tax credit ('CIR' - Crédit d'Impôt Recherche) at 30% on eligible R&D expenditure up to EUR 100,000,000; innovation tax credit ('CII') at 20% on defined innovation outlays capped at EUR 400,000; participation exemption ('régime mère-fille') providing 95% exemption on qualifying dividend receipts with a two-year minimum holding period (Article 145/216 CGI); tax loss carryback ('report en arrière') capped at EUR 1,000,000 generating a refundable tax credit; deduction for creation costs and certain capital allowances for industrial equipment relevant to steel fabrication.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward period ('report en avant') under Article 209-I CGI, with annual utilisation capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the taxable profit exceeding EUR 1,000,000; carryback limited to the previous fiscal year up to EUR 1,000,000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (liasse fiscale, Cerfa n° 11085) together with mandatory schedules 2050 to 2066-SD and Form 2257-SD where transfer pricing documentation is required; electronic filing exclusively through the EFI ('télédéclaration') professional portal of impots.gouv.fr; paper filing is not permitted for CIT purposes and attracts late-filing sanctions.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (declaration de résultat); quarterly prepayment instalments ('acomptes d'IS') are due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December with the final settlement due at the annual filing date.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: General rule: the annual declaration of results must be filed within three months of the close of the fiscal year. For calendar-year SARLs, the statutory filing deadline is the second working day following 1 May of the following year (e.g., 3 May 2024 for the 2023 fiscal year). The balance of CIT is payable on the same date as the annual filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2065-SD, cadre 'Détermination du résultat fiscal et de l'impôt sur les sociétés'
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computes taxable income before and after loss relief, applies the 25% rate (15% on the first EUR 38,120 of profit where the SME conditions are satisfied), and determines the CIT assessed before prepayments are credited.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a French SARL wholly owned by non-residents, verify that no management fees, guarantee fees, or head-office cost allocations are deducted in excess of arm's length levels; evidence the French emploi and operational reality of the EPC steel-structure activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2050-SD / 2051-SD (Bilan actif et passif) with 2054-SD / 2055-SD fixed asset and amortisation tables
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full French statutory balance sheet disclosing fixed assets, inventory (including steel components and prefabricated building work-in-progress), receivables, shareholders' current accounts, provisions, and equity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure French steel inventories are valued at historical cost with correct exchange-rate booking; reconcile retained earnings with the prior year's accepted filing; any interest-bearing current accounts from non-resident shareholders must be documented and priced at arm's length rates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declares the amount of carryforward trading losses, their expiry schedule (unlimited in time), and the utilisation of the EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% excess-profit offset cap.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident groups using a French SARL to shelter losses of the local EPC construction arm must maintain audited schedules proving that losses were generated by genuine French operational activity and not by intra-group margin shifting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2257-SD (état relatif à la documentation des prix de transfert)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual transfer pricing identification statement listing related enterprises, transactions, and confirmation that transfer pricing documentation is held in France.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory where the SARL's annual turnover or total assets reach EUR 400,000,000; the non-resident parent must align the French entity's filing with the group Master File and provide the French tax administration with access to comparable steel-structure distribution and fabrication benchmarking data.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties escalate under Article 1728 CGI: 10% of the tax due where the return is filed late without formal notice or within 30 days of a formal notice; 40% where filed more than 30 days after the formal notice; 80% where not filed at all after formal notice; delayed payment interest accrues at 0.20% per month (2.4% per annum); fraud and deliberate concealment trigger the 80%-100% increase under Article 1729-1729-B CGI; fixed fines of EUR 60 per omitted schedule may also apply; directors are exposed to personal liability where non-filing is a measure of concealment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% withholding tax on gross dividends under Article 119 bis 2 CGI applied to distributions made to non-resident shareholders; relief is available under double-taxation agreements (rates commonly 0%-15%); exemption applies for EU/EEA corporate shareholders satisfying the Parent-Subsidiary Directive conditions under Article 119 ter CGI (direct holding of at least 10% of the French entity's capital for a continuous two-year period); the distributing French SARL also bears the 3% contribution on distributions under Article 235 ter ZCA CGI, which is neutralised or refundable for EU/EEA parent companies qualifying for the directive.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficial owner must obtain a tax residence certificate ('certificat de résidence fiscale') issued by its own tax authority before the distribution date and present it to the French paying entity so the reduced treaty rate is applied at source; the French payer retains the certificate and files the supporting declaration with the tax authorities; for EU parent-subsidiary directive relief, the parent must submit the documentary evidence of its direct 10% holding, a holding-period commitment, and tax residence via the Form 5000/5001 series; if full withholding was applied in error, the excess is recoverable through a formal claim ('réclamation contentieuse', Article R. 196-1 LPF) lodged with the Direction Régionale des Finances Publiques within two years of the distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: French statutory withholding at 33.33% applies to payments of patent, know-how, software, or industrial-property royalties made to non-residents (Article 182 B and related provisions); treaty rates generally reduce the levy to 0%-5%; the EU Interest & Royalties Directive eliminates withholding where the beneficial owner is an EU/EEA company holding at least 25% of the French SARL for two years. Interest: France generally does not impose withholding tax on interest paid to foreign corporate lenders, and the EU Interest & Royalties Directive suppresses the levy for associated EU companies; however, a 75% withholding applies to interest, royalties, or services paid to persons domiciled or established in a non-cooperative State (Article 238 A CGI with Articles 205 A et seq.).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 annual turnover or gross assets for the mandatory French transfer pricing documentation ('documentation sur les prix de transfert') under Article L. 13 AA LPF, including the Local File and group Master File; EUR 750,000,000 consolidated group turnover triggers the French Country-by-Country Report obligations (Article 223 quinquies C CGI); Form 2257-SD must be filed annually by entities meeting the EUR 400,000,000 threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a stand-alone Economic Substance Regulations registry of the Gulf/UAE type, but substantive presence is rigorously enforced through the concepts of 'siège de direction effective' (place of effective management), 'acte anormal de gestion' (abnormal act of management), and the anti-abuse doctrine under Article L. 64 LPF; a French SARL executing steel-structure EPC contracts must maintain real French managerial capacity, payroll, local decisions, risks, and assets, failing which a foreign-controlled 'letterbox' is recharacterised, deductions are denied, and income is reallocated to the actual beneficiaries.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional concealment of taxable French turnover by under-invoicing steel-structure prefab contracts, routing customer payments through an opaque foreign intermediary, or issuing fictitious purchase invoices for construction materials.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal sanctions under Article 1741 of the French General Tax Code (CGI): imprisonment up to 5 years and fine up to EUR 500,000, increased to 7 years and EUR 3,000,000 where committed by an organised group or involving a non-cooperative State; civil tax law penalties of 40%-80% (Article 1729 CGI), late-payment interest at 0.20% per month, confiscation of the fraudulent proceeds, and publication of the conviction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the SARL gérant can be held jointly and severally liable for the company's tax debt under Article L. 267 of the French Book of Tax Procedures for deliberate irregularities; a criminal travel ban ('interdiction de quitter le territoire'), restriction of management rights, personal bankruptcy measures, and, in liquidation, an 'action en comblement de passif' under Article L. 651-2 of the Commercial Code may follow.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance and Artificial Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling prefabricated steel buildings or components to the French SARL at inflated intra-group prices, undercharging French services, stripping margin to a low-tax affiliate, or failing to file the 2257-SD and supporting transfer pricing documentation at the applicable statutory thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation and upward adjustment of the French taxable base under Article 57 CGI; denial of the deduction for undisclosed miss-trust? administrative imposition of the majoration for failure to produce documentation equal to the greater of EUR 10,000 and 5% of the adjustment (Article 1740 A CGI); late-payment interest and penalty increases of 40%-80% for deliberate concealment; reciprocal adjustments may be denied in non-cooperative jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The French gérant personally signs the tax representations; a director who knowingly signs manipulated intercompany steel-supply documentation is exposed to the Article 1741 criminal penalties (5 years imprisonment and EUR 500,000), civil restoration of the understated profit, and use of the corporate veil-piercing doctrine under Article L. 267 LPF; travel bans may be imposed during the penal inquiry.
